newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares up on strong cement, mills trade.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares up on strong cement, mills trade.

text.p: Egyptian share prices rose on Wednesday on the back of strong trading in the cement and milling sectors.
The Capital Market Authority all-share index rose 4.39 points to 359.95 while turnover was a high 81.06 million pounds ($23.88 million).
"Entrance of international securities houses into the Egyptian market has returned investor confidence to the market," said Mohammed Abdallah of Intercapital.
London-based ING Barings are set to take a share in a new Cairo brokerage in partnership with local companies.

Intercapital will manage the new firm whose Egyptian partners include Commercial International Investment Company (CIIC), the investment affiliate of Commercial International Bank (CIB), and Mansour and Maghraby, an investment group with diverse interests.
Amriyah Cement led the way for a strong cement sector in Wednesday's market, closing 0.37 pounds higher at 83.36 after trading in 9.11 million pounds.
Egyptian Tora Portland Cement rose one pound to 90 after shares worth almost four million pounds were traded.
Helwan Portland Cement was the biggest gainer in its sector, closing 1.51 pounds to 72.51 while Suez Cement rose 0.99 pounds to 67.1. Both companies traded in almost two million pounds each.

Chloride Egypt accumulated the most volume, with shares worth 12.5 million pounds changing hands in what brokers said was a direct sale from the Holding Company for Chemical Industries to the an unidentified investor.
The government offered to auction its 38 percent stake or 34,200 shares in Chloride to one or more strategic investors earlier this year. The shares were sold at 365.5 pounds each.
Commerical International Bank (CIB) continued to rally for the third day, climbing 2.91 pounds to 73.01 after trade worth 5.4 million pounds.
Investor disappointment with CIB's announcement last week that it would give out a two pound annual dividend had affected the stock's prices.
Healthy trading in mills continued, with Central and West Delta Flour Mills dominating the sector for the second day. The stock closed 4.18 pounds higher at 90.49.
Mill prices are recovering from investor worries that they would be unable to stand up to competition from the private sector. Abdullah said such fears had been exaggerated.

"The market overreacted to the competition from the private sector. Prices are climbing again because investors have been reassured that it is not that bad and also because of the general overall confidence in the market," he told Reuters.
The index for openly traded firms rose to 509.39 points from 498.28 on Tuesday and that for the rarely-traded "closed" firms increased to 261.78 from 259.91.
Out of 89 shares traded, 43 rose and 21 fell while 25 ended unchanged.
